sources.sourceText: Client-supplied case study: https://claude.ai/artifact/EEQY7aQzr1BZvSDSFHUNh9. Source attribution: Holafly monthly reports, January–August 2026. Underlying reports not supplied or independently audited. User authorized integration on 22 September 2026. 84.3M organic views; 78.8M reported reach; 161 creator partnerships; 920+ content pieces. Cost per thousand reached 56% lower by July versus programme start. Monthly views +169% April–July. August UK 5.10M/+22.5%/27% lower cost; Australia 3.10M/+28.7%/41%; California 3.78M/on target/9%; Saudi Arabia 1.16M/+364%/84%. Cost comparisons in August are against planned cost. Ben Reid previous average ~450K to July 3M+; image is not supplied. Vineyards & Voyages still: 998K views, California. Obaydfox still: 1.01M one reel, Saudi Arabia. Rounded multipliers and blanket exceeded-target claims omitted.

sections.title: Frame. Assemble. Run. Learn.
body: Four connected stages. Your team holds the business context and approval decisions; IRG connects the creator and operating work.

sections.title: Questions to resolve together.
body: Use these points to evaluate the proposed engagement and identify what needs agreement. They are planning questions, not universal contract terms or unverified claims about every campaign.

items.title: Creator suitability
items.body: Which audience, content and brand-suitability checks belong in this brief, and what evidence is available for each recommendation?

items.title: Approval ownership
items.body: Who can approve creators, creative and publication? How will consolidated feedback and approval decisions be recorded?

items.title: Content rights
items.body: Which uses, channels, markets and duration need to be agreed? Is paid usage required, and who confirms the permissions?

items.title: Sponsorship disclosure
items.body: Which disclosure requirements apply to the proposed activity, and who reviews them before publication?

items.title: Reporting ownership
items.body: Who supplies each data source, which definitions will be used, and what limitations should accompany the report?

items.title: Escalation and procurement
items.body: Who is the decision-maker if timing, content or scope changes? Which procurement steps and contracts must be agreed before work starts?

links.label: Discuss scope or procurement requirements
links.linkReason: Supports the next buyer decision in Questions to resolve together.

items.title: How do you measure performance?
items.body: We read the available content and campaign signals against the agreed objective, explain limitations and recommend what to retain, refine or test. Views and reach are not automatically evidence of sales.

items.title: Can you work with our in-house team?
items.body: Yes. Your team holds the business context, internal alignment and approval decisions. IRG connects creator recommendations, coordination, delivery records and interpretation.

items.title: Do we need a finished brief?
items.body: A live brief is useful, but not required. Share the audience problem, operating challenge or performance ambition, along with markets and timing where known.

items.title: What is agreed before a campaign starts?
items.body: The objective, audience, scope, decision-makers, practical requirements and approval points. Rights, disclosure, reporting access and procurement requirements should also be resolved for the proposed activity.

hero.title: 84.3 million organic views for Holafly.
hero.body: An always-on creator programme across the UK, Australia, California and Saudi Arabia, built around continuous sourcing, stronger briefs and repeat partnerships.

sections.title: Programme snapshot.
sections.disclosure: IRG-reported results, attributed to Holafly monthly reports, January–August 2026. The underlying reports were not supplied for independent audit. Organic views are not unique people, sales or incremental impact.

sections.title: From monthly bursts to a connected programme.
body: Holafly’s creator activity was restarting each month. Late activations, availability-led selection and product-heavy briefs made performance difficult to predict, while learning rarely carried into the next campaign.

The brief was to grow reach while reducing cost per thousand reached. IRG focused on the UK, Australia and California, then reactivated Saudi Arabia, with market-specific targets and a consistent operating rhythm.

steps.title: Select for the brief
steps.body: Match creators to market targets and audience relevance. Broaden beyond travel into comedy, family, sport and interviews, reaching nine niches by June.

steps.title: Refresh the creative
steps.body: Rebuild briefs monthly around problem → emotion → product → resolution. Adapt the idea to the creator and their audience.

steps.title: Return and improve
steps.body: Work again with proven creators, carrying performance learning into their next brief.

sections.title: August 2026: targets met or exceeded.
body: These August comparisons use market view targets and planned cost. The cost-below-plan column is different from the programme-start comparison used for the 56% reduction by July.
sections.disclosure: Source attribution: Holafly monthly reports, January–August 2026. Underlying reports not supplied or independently audited.

sections.title: What the evidence supports.
body: The source reports 84.3 million organic views, 78.8 million reported reach, 161 creator partnerships and 920+ content pieces for January–August 2026.
By July, cost per thousand reached was 56% lower than at programme start. Monthly organic views grew 169% from April to July, on a smaller monthly budget than at the start.

The reporting definitions, source files and cross-platform deduplication method have not been provided for independent audit. Reported reach is kept separate from organic views. No sales, conversion, booking or incrementality claim is made.
The programme-level platform mix is not established in the supplied source. One creator example is described as a reel; that alone does not establish the mix for the whole programme.

blockers.details: Existing privacy page contains draft-only text. Accurate policy wording requires the data controller identity, processing purposes, lawful bases where applicable, recipients/processors, retention, rights and contact details to be confirmed. No legal assurances have been invented.

User explicitly requires the existing unfinished resource section and download setup to remain unchanged. No resource content, hide/remove action or download rebuild is included. This is not a launch blocker for this update.

Existing CMS records permission to integrate on 22 September 2026. Preserve exact existing figures and visible source caveats. The reports and full metric definitions are not supplied or independently audited; do not expand the claims, invent ROI or assert client-reviewed new copy.
Leadership biographies, real team imagery, legal entity details and official profiles are not established in the supplied source. Publish only existing positioning and responsibilities.
Programme-level YouTube/Instagram capability, delivery scope and proof have not been confirmed. No platform pages are generated. A reel example does not establish the programme platform mix.
Lifestyle focus is established, but a distinct substantive sector page and client evidence are not supplied. The industry hub links lifestyle buyers to creator selection in the core Services page.

Rights, disclosure, escalation and procurement requirements are represented as questions to resolve for the engagement. No certifications, universal compliance assurances, contract terms or response-time promises are invented.
The existing integration must be retained and tested with intercepted requests or an authorised test sink. No real enquiry should be sent without user authorisation.
